edit.goal.description.md:
Shrink the supply-chain surface: fewer third-party packages reach users and dev machines, and the ones left are deliberate.

Done when `npm i epiq` installs no third-party packages, and every remaining dependency is either core (react, ink, zod, shiki…) or too risky to own (ws, markdown).

Measure with `node source/scripts/dep-stats.mjs`. Before (main 0d6d79a, 2026-11-20):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `npm i epiq`: direct deps | 15 | |
| `npm i epiq`: packages installed | 258 | |
| dev: direct deps | 40 | |
| dev: packages installed | 611 | |
| dev: packages with install scripts | 3 (esbuild, fsevents, node-pty) | |

Largest shipped trees: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 93, react-markdown 82, remark-gfm 68, @pierre/diffs 50, ink 38, remark-breaks 17.

add.issue.name: npm package bundles its dependencies, so `npm i epiq` installs none

edit.description.md:
`build:npm` uses `--packages=external`, so npm users install 258 packages on their own, resolved from version ranges at install time. GUI-only packages (react-markdown, remark-*, @pierre/diffs, react-router-dom, react-dom) are already bundled into dist/gui, but they're still listed under `dependencies`.

- Bundle the Node entries the way the SEA build already does (require shim, devtools stub, NODE_ENV).
- Move every runtime package to `devDependencies`. Users then get the exact versions we locked and tested.
- Fix along the way: `chalk` is a devDependency used at runtime (it only works because ink hoists it); `@xterm/headless` is test-only but listed as runtime.

add.issue.name: CLI parses its flags with node:util parseArgs, not meow

edit.description.md: meow is one call in `source/Index.tsx`. Node's built-in `parseArgs` covers it; the help text is ours already.

add.issue.name: MCP server speaks stdio JSON-RPC itself, without @modelcontextprotocol/sdk

edit.description.md:
The SDK is the largest shipped tree (93 packages: express, hono, cors, jose, ajv, cross-spawn, eventsource…) for HTTP/OAuth transports we never use. We use `McpServer` + `StdioServerTransport`; tests use `Client` + `InMemoryTransport`.

A stdio server is ~300–400 lines: initialize (version negotiation), tools/list, tools/call, ping, notifications. zod 4's `z.toJSONSchema` replaces ajv/zod-to-json-schema. Risk: tracking spec changes. Keep a test against the real SDK client so we notice when the protocol drifts.

add.issue.name: Event ids come from our own ULID module, not the ulid package

edit.description.md: We use `ulid`, `monotonicFactory`, `decodeTime` and `encodeTime` across 43 files. That's ~60 lines on `crypto.getRandomValues`, and these ids order the whole event log, so the code is worth owning. Needs a test comparing it against the package (encoding, monotonic increments, decode) before the swap.

4 files use `createBrowserRouter`, `RouterProvider`, `Navigate`, `useSearchParams` and `useNavigationType`. Replace with a small history/search-param hook, keeping the rule that only back/forward navigation (POP) re-reads URL state. It's bundled into the GUI, so this only reduces build-time exposure.

add.issue.name: Dev installs run no third-party install scripts and skip brand-new versions

edit.description.md:
Install scripts are how the recent npm worms spread. Today 3 packages have them: esbuild, fsevents and node-pty.

Options:
1. `ignore-scripts=true` in `.npmrc`, then explicitly rebuild esbuild and node-pty, and run husky's `prepare` ourselves. Safest, but every install becomes a two-step chore and the hooks can silently go missing.
2. Keep scripts, but add a Dependabot/Renovate cooldown so a version has to be days old before we adopt it. Cheap; catches most worms, which are usually pulled within hours.

Recommend 2 now, and 1 if the dev tree stays large.

eslint-plugin-react pulls in 124 packages, the largest dev tree. Check which of its rules we actually rely on: drop it if hooks + TypeScript cover them, or replace the few that matter with local rules in `eslint-rules.mjs`.

edit.goal.description.md:
Shrink the supply-chain surface: fewer third-party packages reach users and dev machines, and the ones left are deliberate.

Done when `npm i epiq` installs no third-party packages, and every remaining dependency is either core (react, ink, zod, shiki…) or too risky to own (ws, markdown).

Measure with `node source/scripts/dep-stats.mjs`. Before: main 0d6d79a. After: branch `deps/fewer-dependencies` (JQXY3ZR, B76KRK8).

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `npm i epiq`: direct deps | 15 | 0 |
| `npm i epiq`: packages installed | 258 | 0 |
| `npm i epiq`: on disk | 2.5 MB tarball + ~106 MB of deps | 2.8 MB tarball, nothing else |
| dev: direct deps | 40 | 39 |
| dev: packages installed | 611 | 610 |
| dev: packages with install scripts | 3 (esbuild, fsevents, node-pty) | 3 |

Largest trees, now bundled at build time only: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 93, react-markdown 82, remark-gfm 68, @pierre/diffs 50, ink 38, remark-breaks 17. The dev side is what's left: tickets EQWN8S6 (install scripts, cooldown) and AWC4Y5D (lint tree).

add.issue.comment.md:
On branch `deps/fewer-dependencies` (fefe073), not pushed yet.
- New `source/scripts/build-npm.mjs` bundles both bins (require shim, devtools stub, NODE_ENV define). `dependencies` is gone, so `npm i epiq` installs 0 packages, down from 258.
- The React-production e2e is now `npm-bundle.e2e.test.ts`: both bins run from a copy with no node_modules, and the bundle contains React's production build. It fails on the old build and passes on the new.
- Smoke-tested from an isolated dir: TUI renders, `gui` serves, MCP lists 52 tools.
- Trade-off: users no longer pick up dependency patches between our releases, which is exactly what keeps a compromised one out.
